coverage.other_conditions: Residential dwelling unit is defined as any primary residence, excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities.
coverage.summary: Applies to landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken. A residential dwelling unit is defined as any primary residence. Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded. There are no unit-count, building-age or landlord-size limits.
unverifiable_exemptions: Units that are not a primary residence (coverage is limited to primary residences)

evidence.quoted_span: defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities

Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

result.notes: Coverage was largely correct. The ordinance has no unit-count, age or landlord-size limits. I added the primary-residence limitation to unverifiable_exemptions because an address lookup cannot determine whether a unit is someone's primary residence. Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are generally identifiable by property use class, so they remain in other_conditions only. FAIR Act preemption is a conflict issue, not a coverage field, so the preemption-related fields stay null.
